title.narrative: Peace-building with the communities of southern Tolima

description.narrative: Indigenous and campesino communities in the department of Tolima are victims of the conflict in Colombia and struggle to maintain viable livelihoods. Corporacin Grupo Semillas (Semillas) is working with 15 grassroots organizations to implement sustainable agricultural practices, defend their rights to land and water and use communications tools such as community radio to increase the visibility of grassroots resilience and peace-building strategies. At the IAF, we support community-led solutions to enhance peace and security in Colombia. Semillas?s activities bolster community-led efforts to counteract environmental degradation and protect the natural resources that these communities depend on. This grant is part of our broader initiative to build a just and lasting peace in Colombia. Amendment FY19:This amendment provides Grupos Semillas with an additional one year and $82,113 to generate income and increase food security in marginalized rural communities in Southern Tolima by promoting the production and consumption of nutritious local foods, creating seed banks to preserve native seeds, and establishing savings groups through which farmers can obtain microloans. As part of the amendment, Grupos Semillas is working with a network of 18 indigenous and rural organizations and mobilizing an additional $62,844 in counterpart funding to the grant agreement. Amendment FY22:This amendment provides Semillas with an additional 18 months and $294,555 to further strengthen the organizational capacity of 30 social organizations in southwestern Colombia to advance food security, promote the rights of smallholder farmers from Indigenous and Afro-descendent communities, enhance citizen oversight of public and private initiatives, and establish a dedicated fund to promote local women?s and youth-led peacebuilding initiatives.
